title: Quant fidelity hypothesis lab notes — Q1 2025
summary: Working lab notes from the applied-ml quant onboarding run focused on fidelity regressions by micro-slice. This doc collects hypotheses, quick automated results, and prioritized next human-eval passes for AWQ/GPTQ/int8/int4 variants on two candidate models (open-13B and open-7B). The goal: triage which slices are safe to ship with low-precision and which require fallback rules or model-specific calibration.
methodology: We ran the standard onboarding harness (eval-harness v0.9.1, see linked commit) with metric families: task accuracy / exact-match, ROUGE-L for summarization, BLEU for translation/code, and a simple hallucination proxy (entity Hallucination Rate computed via string matching to reference set). Each run used the same prompt-sets and deterministic seed. For human-eval triage we sampled 100 examples per high-risk slice (see action items). Quant variants: fp16 baseline, int8 (Q8), AWQ-int4, GPTQ-int4. Batch size tuned to match latency SLOs, context lengths matched expected production distributions (median 512, tail 4096).
prompt_sets:
Prompt set inventory (names used in harness): 
- ps.open-domain-faqs.v2 (factual QA, short answer)
- ps.multi-step-reasoning.v1 (chain-of-thought style prompts)
- ps.code-synthesis-sparse.v1 (code generation, small functions)
- ps.long-summarization.8k.v1 (8k token summarization/meeting notes)
- ps.dialog-persona.v1 (multi-turn persona consistency)
Notes: ps.multi-step-reasoning includes temperature variations and forced chain-of-thought templates; code-synthesis set contains 30% type-annotated and 70% untyped snippets.
slice_definitions:
Micro-slice taxonomy used for this lab: 
- factual-qa-short: one-sentence factual questions with single entity answers
- multi-step-reasoning: multi-hop reasoning problems (2–4 hops)
- code-gen-small: <30 LOC function synthesis with unit-test gold checks
- long-context-summarization: >3000 token inputs, abstractive summary target
- persona-consistency: dialog turn where model must recall persona facts
- numeric-reasoning: arithmetic/logic with precise numeric outputs
- ambiguous-instruction: under-specified instruction requiring clarification
Each slice has a short sample-set id used in harness (e.g., slice.factual-qa-short.2025q1).
results_overview:
Automated regression highlights across quant variants (baseline fp16). Numbers are approximate deltas vs fp16 on the candidate open-13B model. 
- int8 (Q8): generally small drops, median metric delta -0.6% (accuracy/ROUGE), latency improvement ~1.2x
- GPTQ-int4: modest fidelity hit, median delta -2.2%, but better preserved on arithmetic/numeric reasoning than AWQ in our runs
- AWQ-int4: preservation on embedding-like and short-answer tasks is decent, but we see larger variance; median delta -3.8%, with heavy degradation on long-context summarization and multi-step reasoning
- Notes on open-7B: lower capacity increases sensitivity — AWQ-int4 produced up to -7% on multi-step and -9% on long-context ROUGE-L.
High-level conclusion: int8 is safe to roll for most routes; int4 (both AWQ/GPTQ) needs slice-aware gating and targeted calibration.
per_slice_highlights:
Detailed per-slice anomalies (selected): 
- factual-qa-short: AWQ-int4 delta -1.0% accuracy, GPTQ-int4 delta -0.8%, Q8 delta -0.2% 
- multi-step-reasoning: AWQ-int4 delta -6.1% EM, GPTQ-int4 delta -3.4% EM, Q8 delta -0.9%
- code-gen-small: AWQ-int4 exact-match -5.6% (failures often off-by-one symbol or missing import), GPTQ-int4 -2.9%, Q8 -0.7%
- long-context-summarization: AWQ-int4 ROUGE-L -9.3%, hallucination proxy +7.1pp; GPTQ-int4 ROUGE-L -4.4%, hallucination +2.6pp
- persona-consistency: AWQ-int4 repeated contradictions observed in ~6% of samples vs 1.3% fp16 baseline
- numeric-reasoning: GPTQ-int4 sometimes better than AWQ-int4 (delta +0.4% over AWQ on average) — hypothesis: round-off behavior in AWQ harms multi-step arithmetic chains
Supporting artifacts: sample failure IDs available (slice.fw-ids in linked harness output).
recommended_actions:
Short-term: 
- Do not promote AWQ-int4 to default for routes serving long-context summarization or multi-step reasoning.
- Enable an automatic gating policy: route requests in risky slices to fp16 or int8 by default; allow experimental flag for users to opt in to int4 for cost testing.
- Create a small calibration pass for AWQ (per-layer scaling fix) and re-run multi-step and code-gen slices.
Medium-term: 
- Add slice-aware distillation recipes: fine-tune a lightweight calibration head using 5k examples from multi-step and long-context slices.
- Expand human-eval coverage: 1k samples for long-context summarization across open-13B and open-7B AWQ/GPTQ variants.
Metric changes to monitor: hallucination rate, exact-match, ROUGE-L, and a new token-level drift metric we instrumented in harness.

notes_to_self:
Open threads / hypotheses to probe: 
- Why does AWQ-int4 show larger long-context degradation? suspects: kv-cache quant noise, attention softmax sensitivity, or layernorm quant scaling. Instrument per-layer activation drift.
- GPTQ-int4 seems more stable on numeric chains — confirm across more seeds and different prompt templates.
- Confirm whether code-gen failures are deterministic (same token positions) or stochastic sampling differences.
- Check correlation of latencies with quality regressions (did we mask some slow paths that increased truncation?).
Misc: compile a small golden set of 200 examples for quick smoke checks after any quantizer change.
